evidences.evidence_quote: Existing works mainly capture traditional patterns, such as signal changes due to multi-path effect or mechanical vibrations, for achieving localization[59], user authentication[14], and vibration sensing[36, 60, 64, 66], etc.
evidences.evidence_context: Existing works mainly capture traditional patterns, such as signal changes due to multi-path effect or mechanical vibrations, for achieving localization[59], user authentication[14], and vibration sensing[36, 60, 64, 66], etc. However, no existing works capture electromagnetic variation patterns to achieve RFID-based sensing.

evidences.evidence_quote: Researchers use various sensors, such as accelerator [4, 32], gyroscope [40], Wi-Fi [57], mmWave [5, 30, 31, 55], and RFID [12, 37, 56] to capture speaker/microphone vibration or nearby surface vibration patterns for eavesdropping on speaker-produced or/and human-speaking sound.
evidences.evidence_context: Researchers use various sensors, such as accelerator [4, 32], gyroscope [40], Wi-Fi [57], mmWave [5, 30, 31, 55], and RFID [12, 37, 56] to capture speaker/microphone vibration or nearby surface vibration patterns for eavesdropping on speaker-produced or/and human-speaking sound. However, these methods may be ineffective in noisy environments, as background noise could induce simultaneous physical vibration, leading to significant distortion in recovered sound.
